name: Tarnveil Biolum Suppression Operative Rig
description: Designed explicitly for runners carrying bioluminescent geneware — the subdermal glow, luminous patterning, or light-emitting scales that are fashionable in 2200 but catastrophically conspicuous on a night job. The outer shell is a long-line field jacket in deep tarnished olive, woven with a light-suppression microfibre layer that mutes bioluminescent bleed-through by approximately seventy percent — enough to render a glowing runner dark at practical distances in low light. The jacket is fitted but not tight, falling to upper-thigh, with a pronounced collar that folds up to cover jaw and neck-line bioluminescence. Full-length sleeves have interior biolum-suppression lining as well. The jacket's exterior is matte-finished and treated to resist acid-rain sheeting — a practical nod to Shelf and Circuit-border work. Beneath it, a compression undershirt in the same suppression microfibre handles residual glow from the torso and arms. Trousers are in dark umber cargo-cut with suppression lining in the lower leg panels, plus four concealed pockets accessed through false seam breaks and two thigh-mounted holster channels. The cut is wide enough through the hip and seat to accommodate scaled or furred lower-body geneware without binding. Footwear is a mid-calf boot in matte black synthetic leather with a wrapped ankle cuff that can be extended to knee height for wet terrain, biolum-suppression lining on the inner shaft. A pair of thin suppression gloves in matching olive is stored in the inside chest pocket, extending coverage to the hands. The complete set, worn and closed, reduces visible bioluminescence to near zero in practical field conditions.
materials: tarnished olive biolum-suppression microfibre outer shell
functionality: Approximately 70% bioluminescence muting at practical field distances; acid-rain exterior treatment; full-body coverage system (jacket, undershirt, trousers, boots, gloves); fold-up collar for jaw and neck biolum coverage; concealed false-seam pockets (four in trousers); bilateral thigh holster channels; wide hip-and-seat cut for scaled or furred geneware; extendable boot cuff for wet terrain
what_it_says: This runner has geneware they're proud of — on their own time. On the job, they're disciplined enough to cover it entirely. The tarnished olive reads as practical and slightly military without crossing into costume. Anyone in the runner community who recognizes the suppression microfibre fabric texture knows exactly what this person is and what they're carrying underneath.
worn_by: runners who maintain separate street and job identities
operatives working Shelf or Circuit-border low-light environments
manufacturer: Tarnveil Systems — specialist street label, niche reputation among geneware-heavy runner communities
story_hooks: The suppression microfibre degrades after prolonged acid-rain exposure — a runner's bioluminescent scales start bleeding through the jacket mid-job on a wet Circuit-border rooftop, making them a visible target.

A contact who's never met the runner in person only knows them by their bioluminescent patterning — the runner shows up in full Tarnveil suppression and the contact refuses to confirm identity, stalling the handoff.

The suppression gloves are one size too small for a runner with scaled hands from geneware, and removing them mid-job to operate delicate equipment lights up their hands like a beacon in the dark corridor.

physical_description.visual_profile: A complete tactical suppression kit that reads as dark, purposeful, and deliberately muted. The long-line field jacket dominates the silhouette, creating a lean vertical emphasis despite its practical bulk. The pronounced collar and full-length sleeves suggest maximum coverage. Overall impression: professional operative, intentionally invisible.
physical_description.fit: Fitted but unrestricted through the torso and shoulders; deliberately relaxed through hips, seat, and thighs to accommodate geneware without binding. The cargo trousers sit at natural waist with a slight drop through the leg. Compression undershirt hugs the body beneath the jacket. Boots anchor the look with a substantial, grounded stance.
physical_description.primary_material: Deep tarnished olive ballistic weave outer shell treated with acid-rain resistant coating; dark umber cargo cotton-synth blend for trousers; matte black synthetic leather boots; suppression microfibre lining throughout (interior and integrated panels). Gloves in matching olive suppression weave.
physical_description.texture: Matte-finished, non-reflective surfaces throughout. The outer jacket has a subtle gridded texture from the biolum-suppression weave. Trousers feel structured and utilitarian. Boots have a sealed, weatherproof finish. Gloves are thin and precise, designed for dexterity.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep muted palette: tarnished olive dominant, dark umber trousers, matte black boots and undersuit. No bright accents or reflective trim. The suppression microfibre creates subtle shadow-play in fabric texture.
physical_description.closures: Full-length dual-track zipper down the jacket front with storm flap; magnetic snap collar points; false seam break closures on cargo pockets (friction-fit); thigh holster channels with friction retention; wrapped ankle cuff secured with velcro for extension; elastic retention on glove storage pocket.
distinctive_features: Integrated biolum-suppression microfibre throughout all layers and panels — the core feature
Pronounced collar that extends to jaw/neck coverage when folded up
Four concealed thigh pockets accessed through false seam breaks — anti-snag design
Two dedicated holster channels on thighs with friction-lock retention
Extendable ankle cuff on boots — transitions mid-calf to knee height for wet terrain
Interior compression undershirt built into kit composition
Stored suppression glove pair in chest pocket for quick deployment
Acid-rain treated exterior finish — practical wear indicator: mild dulling/patina over time
No branding visible — Tarnveil Systems logo is subtle embroidered tag inside collar only
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 functional equipment. Affordable enough for working-class runners, specialized enough to signal street credibility. Not corpo luxury, not salvage tier — purpose-built working gear.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street runner culture, geneware-heavy communities, night-operation specialists, Shelf and Circuit border workers. Wearing this signals: 'I have augmentations I need to hide, I work in the dark, I need to move unseen.' It's the uniform of people who understand that bioluminescence is fashionable until it gets you killed.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn-in, not distressed. Field-ready. Typical patina: subtle acid-rain dulling on the jacket shoulders and upper back; minor scuffing on boot heels and cuffs; fabric creasing at elbows and knees from active use. No tears or patches — Tarnveil gear is designed for durability. Gloves show fingertip wear. The look is professional, maintained, used.
